title: Wearing the Shoes of Someone Who Passed Away
summary: This class explores the traditional practice and halakhic discussions surrounding the use of clothing and shoes belonging to a deceased person. Rabbi Harari examines various sources, including Sefer Hasidim and the writings of contemporary authorities, to determine whether these items are forbidden or if they can be donated to charity. The discussion addresses whether concerns about health, hygiene, or mystical omens should influence how families handle the belongings of a loved one.
questions: Is it forbidden to wear the shoes of a person who has passed away?
Can I donate the clothing of a deceased family member to charity?
Does the prohibition against using a deceased person's shoes apply to all types of footwear?
Is the concern about wearing a deceased person's shoes based on mysticism or health concerns?
Are there specific circumstances where it is recommended to avoid using the belongings of the deceased?
